resources.string: Every gesture decoded by the DEV keyboard is written to a file on this device, including the words it produces. Nothing leaves the device and nothing is sent anywhere. This build exists to capture that file; the normal Duet build records nothing.

Word traces keep every touch sample of each word together with the word that was committed, so the decoder can be replayed and measured off the device. They are on by default in this developer build and can be switched off here; practice mode records while it is open either way. Private fields and fields that ask for no learning are never recorded. Nothing leaves the device unless you export it.

Swipe or tap the word shown with the Duet DEV keyboard, then space, three times per word. Each attempt is recorded with the shown word as its label, for measuring the decoder. If you know an attempt went wrong, tap Discard last swipe and do it again. Recording stops when you leave this screen.
Attempt %1$d of %2$d · %3$d recorded, %4$d decoded as shown
This passage: %1$d of %2$d words, %3$d as shown · Done: %4$d passages, %6$d of %5$d words as shown

Type the passage above with the Duet DEV keyboard, as you would type a message: swipe or tap, with or without automatic spaces, capitals and punctuation as you like. The word to type is underlined; finished words turn green when they came out as shown and red when not. Each word is recorded with the passage word as its label. To withdraw a bad attempt, tap Discard last swipe right after it, then delete the word and type it again. Recording stops when you leave this screen.
On: model %1$s, beta %2$s. The spacebar shows NN while it is on.
Off: the keyboard decodes exactly as the normal build.
The model is missing from this build, so the rerank cannot be switched on.
Rerank on this phone: p50 %1$s ms, p95 %2$s ms over %3$d decodes

Reorders the decoder\'s top 50 by how well a small swipe network, trained on FUTO\'s public swipe dataset, reads the path. It runs on this phone with no network. Practice mode always decodes each attempt both ways and shows which one got the word, whether this is on or off; each attempt\'s trace line keeps both answers.

Decides whether a tapped word then a swipe, or a word typed on after its automatic space was taken back, is one word or two with one model fitted on your traces, instead of fixed ratios. On by default in this build. The decode log marks its calls \"(model)\".

Now and then (at most every five minutes), after you undo a word and type a close one instead, the bar asks whether the first word was meant as the second. Your answer goes into the word trace as a confirmed label, so replay measures on what you meant rather than a guess.

Ranks words by a real language model (how likely the word is after the last two) plus a shape fit that never goes flat, instead of today\'s score. On by default in this build since the 2026-11-18 phone batch: with the switches below it read 85 words in 100 right against 81 for today\'s score. The release build keeps today\'s score.

Reads every tap as each key near it, charged by how far the touch is from that key, instead of the key under your finger unless the list runs short. Best with the language-model score. On by default in this build.
Counts a miss more where your thumb was slow (a key you meant) and less where it was flying past. Best with the language-model score. On by default in this build.

Two or three words gestured with no space between them are read as separate words when that fits better than one word. The first word is committed with a space and the rest stays in hand. Works with automatic spaces off. Needs the language-model score. On by default in this build.

A second neural model that watches both thumbs in time re-scores the suggestions. Needs "Language-model score" on. In replay it fixed about four in a hundred words on top of everything else. It runs only when the top two suggestions are close, and adds about 10 ms then on a computer, more on a phone.

When the word you type next shows the word before it was read wrong (\"tot he\" for \"to the\"), the earlier word is corrected in place. One backspace right after puts it back, and a fix you undo is not made again. Needs the language-model score. On by default in this build.
Comparison unavailable until the keyboard has loaded its dictionary.
